I Never rested on the Muses bed,
Nor dipt my pen in her deep thought,
But to your worthy praise I'll bend,
And sing the praise of Drummond's thought.

This humble verse, though far from great,
Is offered to your noble name,
And may it find a place in fate,
To share the honor of your fame.

Though I may stumble in my rhyme,
And falter in my feeble song,
Yet let it be a worthy time,
A tribute to your noble tongue.

So here's to you, dear Drummond, friend,
Whose words have touched my heart and mind,
And may your poetry never end,
A shining light for all to find.
